api.notes: The trigger: the first element of the default slot. A text-only body makes the element itself the trigger (focusable, dashed underline).

api.reason: A React ref object. The slotted trigger is the anchor (it is also the popover's implicit CSS anchor); to anchor to an element that is not the trigger, wrap that element. See TOOLTIP-02.

api.notes: Attribute and property, plain text. See TOOLTIP-01.
Inverted: `isEnabled={false}` is `disabled`, so the boolean attribute defaults to off.
Cancelable, carries `open` and `reason` (hover, focus, escape, touch, outside). Preventing it vetoes the change; property writes never emit it.
The `open` attribute at first render; the tooltip stays dismissible.
Controlled use: listen to `tct-open-change`, `preventDefault()` and set `open` yourself. The read-only `isOpen` getter reports whether the layer is on the stack.
`show()` and `hide()` open and close it programmatically (no tct-open-change).

hooks.notes: Layer stack membership, Escape, hint kind, anchor positioning through PositionController.
Escape and outside presses go through the shared layer stack: the tooltip closes before its dialog.
touch-trigger auto | tap | none, in packages/core/src/controllers/tooltip.ts.

keyboard.action: Shows the tooltip after keyboard focus (focus-visible), when the trigger is naturally focusable or focus-trigger is always.
Hides the tooltip, and only the tooltip: an enclosing dialog or popup stays open (WCAG 1.4.13, IME-guarded).

differences.text: `content` is a string. Upstream accepts a ReactNode; rich tooltip content is not offered because the popup is a satellite whose text becomes the trigger's accessible description, which has to be plain text.
`anchorRef` is not ported: references to elements across the page are a React device, and the trigger is the anchor. Wrap the element you want to describe.

`isOpen` and `isDefaultOpen` are one `open` property: it is the state, the attribute sets it initially, and a controlled tooltip vetoes changes in `tct-open-change` and writes `open` itself. `isEnabled` is inverted to `disabled`.

The popup is an owned light-DOM satellite (`tct-tooltip-surface`, popover=manual, role=tooltip) next to the trigger, so `aria-describedby` resolves without crossing a shadow root; it works with Tier-2 browsers, where element reflection is missing.

Positioning uses CSS anchor positioning (the trigger is the popover's implicit anchor); Floating UI is loaded only where that is unavailable or `implicitAnchor` is forced off. The trigger must be a single element or text.

The surface keeps the inverted look and 300px cap of tct-button's built-in tooltip (styles/layer.styles.css): primary-text fill, surface-colour ink, container radius, no shadow. Tecton has no tooltip design; entry is a fade only, because a tooltip must not move while the pointer travels to it.

provisional: Entry is a fade with no movement; upstream nudges the surface away from the trigger.
core.tooltip.notes: Guides: [mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips] hover and focus intent with a hide bridge; [mwg:position-aware-tooltips] implicit anchor positioning with a Floating UI fallback and a flipped `data-placement`; [mwg:accessible-web-components] the description is wired with ids in one tree; [mwg:animate-to-from-top-layer] exit animation through WAAPI before hiding the popover (never `overlay`). Exports are TOOLTIP_SIDES / TooltipSide (not TOOLTIP_PLACEMENTS / TooltipPlacement) because text/text.types.ts already exports those names.
